Projects I worked on during my Research Master's in Economics at Sciences Po.

## Papers {.research-section}

::: {.paper}
[[Replication of *Wage Stagnation and the Decline of Standardized Pay Rates* (Massenkoff & Wilmers, 2023)](Replication_Massenkoff_and_Wilmers_2023.qmd)]{.paper-title}

[Labor Economics, taught by Pierre Cahuc]{.paper-meta}

::: {.paper-links}
[PDF](Labor_replication.pdf){.paper-btn}
[Original paper](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/app.20200819){.paper-btn}
[More](Replication_Massenkoff_and_Wilmers_2023.qmd){.paper-btn}
:::

<details>
<summary>Summary</summary>
I replicate this paper on the drivers of blue-collar wage stagnation in the US in the 1970s–1990s, conducting robustness checks and extensions. In line with the authors, I find that the decline of standardized pay rates contributed significantly to wage stagnation. I further show that the decline was driven almost entirely by firms moving away from fully standardized pay structures, rather than from tenure-based pay.
</details>
:::

::: {.paper}
[[Modelling Class Attendance as a Game of Strategic Interactions between Students](Micro_Group_Project.pdf)]{.paper-title}

[Group project · Microeconomics 2, taught by Emeric Henry]{.paper-meta}

::: {.paper-links}
[PDF](Micro_Group_Project.pdf){.paper-btn}
:::

<details>
<summary>Summary</summary>
A game theory paper exploring the determinants of class attendance as a game of strategic interactions between students. In a final extension, we introduce a teacher as a special player, who uses students' strategies to set her own.
</details>
:::

::: {.paper}
[[*The Wealth Inequality of Nations* (Pfeffer & Waitkus, 2021)](Pres_Macro.pdf)]{.paper-title}

::: {.paper-links}
